# A raw HTML element resolves to the `element` component sngl:platform/html
# declares, so a call against it is checked like any other. Before, the
# platform's Resolve() minted a nameless component with no props and the
# checker skipped validation entirely: every prop name and every value passed.

# An attribute nobody declared and no wildcard covers is an error. The tail
# covers lowercase attribute names, so a camelCase one — a DOM property, not an
# attribute — misses it unless `element` declares it.
! sngl check badname.sngl
stderr 'unknown prop "innerTxt" on component element'

# A declared attribute's type is checked. `style` is a struct, not a string.
! sngl check badtype.sngl
stderr 'cannot use string as Style for prop "style" on component element'

# `tag` names the element to emit — the escape hatch for a tag no identifier
# can spell — and is not itself an attribute.
sngl generate --platform html --lang none -o out custom.sngl
grep '<my-widget' out/index.html
! grep 'tag="my-widget"' out/index.html

# An ordinary tag still emits its own name.
grep '<div' out/index.html

-- badname.sngl --
import . "sngl:app"
import "sngl:platform/html"

component main {
    window {
        html.div(innerTxt = "x")
    }
}
-- badtype.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"
import "sngl:platform/html"

component main {
    window {
        html.button(style = "wide")
    }
}
-- custom.sngl --
import . "sngl:app"
import "sngl:platform/html"

component main {
    window {
        html.div {
            html.element(tag = "my-widget", innerText = "hi")
        }
    }
}
